reason: Trial 2 is the strongest completed PRIMARY result (macro_f1 0.92965) using MiniLM plus lexical features, but its spam recall is 0.7802 and score gap is 0.0327. The nonlinear lexical candidate extends the same encoder/feature family with an RBF expansion, making it the most direct next test of whether nonlinear feature interactions improve macro_f1 on the primary split.
review: Trial 1 word-only logistic had macro_f1 0.46304 with spam recall 0.0, so simple word features are inadequate. Trial 2 is much stronger but still leaves spam recall below ham recall. The proposed candidate is untried and uses the registered logistic classifier; no causal or guaranteed improvement is claimed.
hypothesis: A nonlinear RBF expansion over word/char lexical features plus frozen MiniLM embeddings may capture interactions that the linear MiniLM lexical model misses, potentially improving spam recall and macro_f1 on the primary split.
uncertainty: The direction and magnitude of change are unknown. Nonlinear expansion may overfit, increase the train-search gap, or fail to improve spam recall. Only training-derived PRIMARY evidence is available; no formal test is available to the agent.
